claim: The text encodes one or more natural languages
distinctive_prediction: a compact morphology and syntax generalize across unseen folios
minimum_test: hand- and section-held-out parsing against matched languages
failure_condition: rules or meanings change by passage and require many exceptions

claim: The text is enciphered natural language
distinctive_prediction: one fixed reversible system yields grammatical full lines and external anchors
minimum_test: predeclared cipher and language tested on sealed folios
failure_condition: only selected words read or nulls/homophones grow after errors

claim: Glyph groups are dense medieval abbreviation or shorthand
distinctive_prediction: expansions follow attested rules consistently and predict unseen forms
minimum_test: compare with dated genre-matched abbreviation corpora
failure_condition: expansion choices are unconstrained or unique to each token

claim: A designed language or encoding generated the text
distinctive_prediction: a small explicit rule set predicts distributions and unseen strings

claim: The writing was generated without propositional semantic content
distinctive_prediction: a simple generator reproduces local and global effects across sections
minimum_test: copy-mutate and layout-aware generators tested on untuned statistics
failure_condition: generator misses hand/section/position structure or is more complex than rivals

claim: Different sections or text types use different mechanisms
distinctive_prediction: independently defined partitions require stable distinct models
minimum_test: predeclare partitions from codicology before textual fitting
failure_condition: partitions are added only to rescue errors
